newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - Colombia, Brazil spreads gain.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - Colombia, Brazil spreads gain.

text.p: Mounting concern over scarce prompt coffee supplies gave a sharp boost to Colombian and Brazilian differentials this week, trading sources said.
"No doubt about it, spot coffee is very tight," one dealer said. "And nearby differentials are going up."

Spot Colombian Excelsos were discussed at 24 cents over the CSCE December contract, up a hefty four cents from last week. Brazilian Santos 4s, which netted two cents under "C" a week ago, were offered at one cent over "C".
Stocks of exchange-deliverable coffee fell to a fresh 12-year low last week, while U.S. consumer stocks are hovering at their lowest levels since the mid-1980's.

While the current supply jitters should begin to ease when new-crop coffee starts to flow in from Latin America, reports that Mexico's crop could be delayed due to heavy rains could prolong the supply crunch, dealers said.
In addition, key Central American producers Guatemala and Costa Rica may be facing weather-related crop delays of their own, they said.
For now, dealers said most roasters appeared generally well-supplied, and cheaper prices on forward deliveries kept a lid on prompt sales.
"Most roasters are well covered through October," a trader said. "They knew there wouldn't be any coffee until November or December."
Refleflecting expectations for more plentiful supplies in the coming months, dealers said forward differentials remained steady at a steep discount to spot rates.
Colombian MAMS for November-December delivery were heard at 14 to 16 cents over the board, some 10 cents below the spot premium.
CSCE December coffee rose 1.35 cents a lb Thursday, to settle at 114.90. March ended 0.95 higher, at 106.80.
